doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Billie's sisters as singers and blues
summary: The sisters all sang; Edna, Della and Billie loved blues while Sadie and Ida preferred sentimental songs.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Did your sister sing much by the way? Oh yeah, all my sisters sing.
They all got beautiful voice. Beautiful voice. They said it here. All of them, Ida, they all got nice voice. They all had nice voice. They said it was the best. I mean, you know.

See, they more sing that, uh, channel voice, like you know, all the nice songs, you know, really nice, sentimental songs like that. He didn't sing no variety blues. That's everything I ever did, like singing about blues. Yeah, but I mean Sadie. No, Sadie never sing no blues. Sadie never sing no blues. Sadie never sing no blues. Sadie and Ida never cared about singing any blues. They never did. But Edna, Dalla and myself, we love blues. I love to sing blues. That's true. I don't believe Ida and Sadie can sing blues. I don't, I'm telling you too, I don't believe I ever heard sing blues. I know Edna loves blues. Edna loves blues. She sing them too. She can rather blues. I know Edna, myself and Dalla, we sing the blues all the time. But I and Sadie, I never have to sing no blues. Never they have to sing no blues. Sadie sing classical music, all them nice, you know, she got a pretty voice.

Well, you ought to get your sisters to sing blues here in the town. Maybe make some recordings of them. They not here. Well, they might pass by to see you sometime. You never know. Nobody left but Edna, huh? No, I have three. I know, but I mean they sing the blues. Edna, Edna's the only one.

You're the Edna. Yeah, Edna. And she can sing them too. She can better get the same. Now that's who ought to be, y'all. Oh, Edna give y'all so much stuff and be a pity. Y'all get tired, I bet you. Oh, yeah. She can talk a plenty, she experienced. Traveling a lot. Sure, she don't talk a lot. She's traveling a lot. Sure, she don't talk a lot. I mean, D and I got married. Edna came to New Orleans here to visit me. And I haven't saw Edna for 25 years. 25 years until she came to New Orleans to see me. She was gone.
And I worked with her in town. Yeah. I was trying to care. You worked with her, yeah. And she worked with me then. Who was in town? Well, Edna's the good company.
In fact, I worked with, I worked with Artie, your sister. Yeah, you worked with, I worked with you.
I worked with all of my sisters.
I worked with every one of them. Edna, Artie, and Sadie.
